newsitem.title: PERU: French climbers feared killed in Peruvian Andes.
newsitem.headline: French climbers feared killed in Peruvian Andes.

text.p: Peruvian rescuers were searching on Thursday for two French climbers missing for four days and feared dead after reportedly falling into a ravine in the Andes, officials said.
Fellow hikers reported the pair were scaling the 19,540- foot (5,960 metre) Mount Alpamayo in northern Peru when nails came loose on an ice-face and they fell 650 feet (200 metres) down a ravine.
Local authorities were using helicopters and rescue patrols to comb the area in the hope of finding the climbers alive.
"We are trying to see what we can do but unfortunately it's a very inaccessible region," local official Rember Ceballos said.

The incident followed the deaths last Friday of a French climber and a Peruvian guide caught by an avalanche in the same Cordillera Blanca or White Range of mountains. A U.S. alpinist died Saturday in the same range after a heart attack.
